top_categories.workout_context: 636 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
At Race Across Portugal, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
41,010ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
64ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Race Across Portugal's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 636 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
636 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 41,010ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Race Across Portugal. Train it until it feels boring.
41,010ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Road-specific control matters at Race Across Portugal. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 636 miles.
Low-cadence force work supports 41,010ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: March in Vila Meã, Amarante, Porto District, Portugal. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Race Across Portugal. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: For a multi-day 636-mile race, no single calorie total or one-food strategy is credible. Rehearse continuous intake while riding plus substantial meals at planned stops; document carbohydrate, fluid, and sodium intake, resupply cadence, and gut response. Use checkpoints and publicly available services only as the category rules allow, carry backup calories, and complete a full night-riding systems rehearsal.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Race Across Portugal. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Over Under, and Mixed Climbing to prepare you for 636 miles of mixed terrain in Vila Meã, Amarante, Porto District, Portugal.
